sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Basis**: Established in 2003 under the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**, headquartered in **Chennai**.
• **Core Mandate**: Facilitate, regulate, and advise the Government of India on matters relating to the conservation of biodiversity, sustainable use of its components, and equitable sharing of benefits.
• **Institutional Hierarchy**: Operates through a three-tier structure: **NBA (National)**, **SBB (State Biodiversity Boards)**, and **BMC (Biodiversity Management Committees)** at the local level.
• **Key Metric**: The **Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS)** mechanism ensures that benefits derived from the utilization of biological resources are shared with the local communities who act as custodians.

items.definition: A comprehensive document recording local knowledge of biological resources and traditional practices, maintained by BMCs. It is the primary tool for legal claims in ABS.
The legal framework requiring users of biological resources to share the benefits (monetary or non-monetary) with the providers (local communities) as per the Nagoya Protocol.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **IPR Approval**: Prior approval of NBA is mandatory before applying for any Intellectual Property Rights (patents) based on biological resources from India.
• **PBR Digitization**: National-level push to digitize PBRs to create a searchable database for researchers and policymakers.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of awareness at the Panchayat level, delays in ABS fund disbursement, and conflict between development projects and biodiversity conservation.
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the capacity of BMCs, simplifying the ABS application process, and integrating PBRs with digital land records.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: '3-Tier-ABS'
• **Decoded Meaning**: 3-Tier (NBA-SBB-BMC), A (Access), B (Benefit), S (Sharing). Remember: NBA is the 'Gatekeeper' for foreigners; SBB is the 'Regulator' for locals.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the role of NBA with the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL). Remember: NBA deals with biological resources/traditional knowledge; NBWL deals with wildlife/protected areas.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Bio-piracy' when discussing the importance of NBA in protecting indigenous traditional knowledge from unauthorized patenting.

keyTakeaways: NBA is a statutory body under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
Prior approval of NBA is mandatory for IPR applications involving Indian biological resources.
BMCs are the backbone of the Act, responsible for maintaining People's Biodiversity Registers (PBR).
